newsitem.title: USA: UPS says strike threat affecting business.
newsitem.headline: UPS says strike threat affecting business.

text.p: United Parcel Service of America Inc., the nation's largest package distribution company, said Thursday the threat of a strike by unionized employees has begun to affect its business in the United States.

Last week, the Teamsters union polled its 185,000 members at UPS for permission to call a strike if contract talks fail to produce a new agreement by midnight July 31. Union officials later said results showed the strike authorisation vote had been approved by 95 percent of those who voted.
UPS said it viewed the vote as a commonplace tactic of labour negotiations. But a spokesman said the vote has worried some UPS clients.

"We've already had some customers who've said if the situation isn't resolved by the 31st, they're going to divert some volume. We have some that have already done so," UPS spokesman Mark Dickens said.
"It has not been a significant amount at this point ... but I know it will probably accelerate as we get closer to the 31st if things have not been finalised."
The Teamsters represent about two-thirds of the company's domestic payroll, including delivery truck drivers, tractor-trailer drivers and package facility workers.
During negotiations in 1993, the Teamsters bargained a month past the July 31 deadline before going to a strike authorisation vote.
But union officials this time have been sharply critical of the Atlanta-based company for not advancing serious proposals, a charge UPS denies.
